summary: At 88 square miles, Fremont is physically larger than San Francisco — a fact that surprises almost everyone who pictures it as just another East Bay suburb. That sprawl matters: the city stretches from the tidal marshes along the San Francisco Bay's eastern shore all the way up into the golden-grass foothills of the Diablo Range, meaning the western neighborhoods sit on pancake-flat former salt flats while the eastern edges climb into Mission Peak, whose 2,517-foot summit delivers one of the most photographed Bay Area panoramas. Tesla's massive Fremont factory and a cluster of tech, semiconductor, and advanced-manufacturing firms make this a genuine job center, not merely a bedroom community, though I-880 commutes toward San Jose or Oakland remain notoriously congested. The median household income of $176,350 is high by national standards, yet a median home price above $1.28 million puts the price-to-income ratio around 7.3 — meaning even at that elevated income, ownership requires significant down-payment capital or dual earners. Daily life is more strip-mall-and-boulevard than walkable-downtown, with commercial activity strung along auto-oriented corridors like Fremont Boulevard rather than a single coherent core; the tradeoff is generous park acreage, miles of bay trail access, and mild year-round temperatures averaging 70°F highs with roughly nine hours of daily sunshine. Fremont is essentially an entire mid-sized city hiding inside the Bay Area's shadow, offering real employment density and open-space access at the cost of the pedestrian urbanity its price tag might lead you to expect.
